"Reform UK and Tories attack Burnham's triple lock pension move"
Reform UK and Tory leaders have hit out at Burnham's plans to drop the triple lock in a future Labour manifesto, setting up a clash on a policy previously backed by all major parties. The commitment could put Labour's support at risk given widespread support among older voters.
ROBERT JENRICK, Reform UK Treasury spokesman: the pledge was "just mean".
NIGEL FARAGE, Reform leader: Burnham would "abdicate his responsibility to British pensioners"; "If he is so desperate to pick a fight with pensioners, he should get on with it, call a general election now, and let the public decide."
KEMI BADENOCH, Conservative leader: the proposal was "falling apart under scrutiny" and would not provide enough funds for a care system, "which means more tax rises are inevitable". On state control of utilities: "Burnham wants to take Britain back to the 1970s, a time of more government control, more trade union control and no economic growth. There is a reason our country took a different course after that decade."
Note: the article records the awkwardness for Badenoch's Conservatives, which have pledged more than £20bn in welfare savings.
